answer: A grove of agents can resist sybil attacks by requiring stake-backed identity: each agent locks a small deposit tied to one verifiable credential before it can trade. Like a comet leaving a traceable trail, every action is signed and logged, so fake identities cannot hide. Reputation then grows like a nebula, slowly, from many independent peer attestations, so a swarm of fresh unvouched accounts carries no weight while long-lived agents with proven history do.
